## Pet Groomer Marketing Case Study: Driving Success With Digital Ads

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13120320/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-featured.webp)

Why is a smart digital advertising strategy a game-changer for pet groomers?

In this digital age, your potential customers are all online. They’re looking for trustworthy, top-quality pet services right there on their smartphones and computers. And, you want to be the answer they find.

The magic of digital ads is in their super-targeting abilities. You don’t want to be advertising to just anyone, right? You want to find pet owners, those in your service area or people showing interest in pet grooming services.

Maybe you even specialize, say, in poodles. You can tune your ads to find the exact people you want to reach. It’s like having a megaphone that only reaches the ears of those who are actually interested in what you’ve got to say!

The other cool thing about digital marketing is picking your channels. You see, not every pet owner is the same. Some might be searching on Google, while others are scrolling their Facebook feeds or watching YouTube videos.

Each channel offers different opportunities to connect with customers, so it’s important to know where your audience hangs out online.

To top it all off, digital ads let you measure success in real-time. You get to see which channels are doing well, which audience targeting is working and then adjust on the fly. No more guessing or waiting to see if your ad in the local paper worked.

To put it simply, smart digital advertising helps pet groomers connect with the right pet owners, at the right time and in the right places. It’s a game-changer, really!

## Local business drives success with smart digital advertising

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115903/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-clicks-conversions.webp)

One mobile pet grooming business with locations across the country has seen the power of smart digital advertising first hand.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115918/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-overview.webp)

Over the past six months, they’ve seen millions of impressions, hundreds of thousands of clicks and tens of thousands of conversions. And, much of their success is thanks to their effective digital advertising strategy.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115920/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-period-report.webp)

Compared to the previous 6-month period, this mobile pet groomer had a 134% increase in impressions, a 696% increase in clicks and a 682% increase in conversions.

### How did they do it?

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115902/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-ads-overall.webp)

This mobile pet groomer’s advertising strategy started with identifying their target audience and where they spend their time online. This helped them choose the right channels to advertise on — Facebook and Google.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115916/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-brand-awareness-1024x628.webp)

On Facebook, they built a strategy focused on building a recognizable brand. This not only helped them get their name out there, but it also helped to build trust with potential customers.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115923/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-targeting.webp)

They also made it a point to target their advertising strategy to the right audience. By targeting lookalike audiences, as well as potential customers based on their location and interests, they got in front of people most likely to be interested in their services.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115905/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-facebook-video-ad.webp)

They also ran video ads on Facebook, helping their message stand out on a highly competitive platform.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115921/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-search-ad.webp)

In addition to advertising on Facebook, they also drove pet groomer leads with Google search ads.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115912/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-ad-kewyords.webp)

By bidding on the right keywords, they were able to get in front of people actively searching for pet grooming services in their service areas.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115909/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-location-page.webp)

Finally, they improved their conversion rate by directing their ads to landing pages optimized for the same local keywords in their ads.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115907/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-keyword-performance.webp)

Not only did this help them convert more leads, but it also helped them increase their organic visibility on search engines for long-tail keywords and their organic traffic.

![](https://d357wx87z4hzhv.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/13115910/pet-groomer-marketing-case-study-traffic.webp)

### Conclusion

Smart digital advertising is like a secret weapon for pet groomers. By finding the right audience and connecting with them on their favorite online platforms, you can supercharge your reach and make your business the go-to choice for pet owners in your area.

# How much does grooming salon marketing cost?

Oct 24, 20267 min readPerform Pets Team

**Grooming salon marketing from an agency that works with pet businesses costs about $750 to $5,000 or more a month for ongoing work in 2026, based on [a November 2026 review of 46 pet and veterinary agency websites](https://performpets.com/what-pet-and-veterinary-marketing-agencies-charge-in-2026/). Ad spend is paid to Google or Meta on top of that fee. A salon that runs its own marketing pays mainly for ads and the booking software it already uses.**

Few agencies publish prices, so those figures come from the three that do, checked on October 14, 2026. They are the range those agencies list, not an industry average, and larger or multi-location engagements can cost more. Perform Pets is one of the agencies in the table, and our price is listed the same way as the others. This article covers what each part costs, what a click and a lead cost in the pet category, and how to set a budget from what a grooming client is worth over a year.

## What does grooming salon marketing cost each month?

It depends on which parts you buy and who does the work. These are published prices from each company’s own website. Scopes differ, so compare what is included, not only the number.

| What you are buying | Published price | Published by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ongoing multi-channel package | $997 to $3,247 a month across three tiers; the top tier has entry requirements | TailWerks |
| Ongoing multi-channel package | From $2,000 a month, one location | Perform Pets |
| Ongoing partnership | Generally from $2,500 a month | Pet Engine Marketing |
| Paid ads program | Management fee not published; requires at least $600 a month in ad spend | Paw Point Marketing |

Ad spend is not included in any of these fees. Check each agency’s minimum term and what its entry tier leaves out before comparing prices. Separate from the monthly fee, these one-time and software costs are published too:

| One-time or software cost | Published price | Published by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Website build | $3,000 once | Perform Pets |
| Branded website build | From $7,600 once | Pet Marketing Unleashed |
| Booking software, mobile grooming plans | $49 to $159 a month; the higher plans are priced per van | MoeGo |

These are MoeGo’s mobile plans; salon plans and other grooming software vary, so check what reminders and messaging your current plan already includes. A wider list of agencies is in [best pet marketing agencies in 2026](https://performpets.com/best-pet-marketing-agencies-2026/).

## What does the whole monthly bill look like?

Add up every line, not only the agency fee. Three common setups:

*   **Doing it yourself.** Ad spend, booking software you likely already pay for, and your own hours.
*   **Agency plus ads.** The management fee, ad spend paid to Google or Meta, and your software.
*   **New website plus ongoing marketing.** A one-time build, then the fee, ad spend and software each month.

As an example from the prices above, a $2,000 fee plus $600 in ad spend is $2,600 a month before software.

## What are the parts of a grooming marketing budget?

Five. A quote that looks low has usually left one of them out.

*   **Management fee.** What an agency or freelancer charges to plan and run the work.
*   **Ad spend.** What you pay Google or Meta for the ads. It is separate from any fee and should be billed to an account in your name.
*   **Website.** A build cost, then hosting and upkeep.

Title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns

URL Source: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118

Markdown Content:
Quality Score is a diagnostic tool meant to give you a sense of how well your [ad quality](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/156066) compares to other advertisers.

This score is measured on a scale from 1-10 and available at the keyword level. A higher Quality Score means that your ad and landing page are more relevant and useful to someone searching for your keyword, compared to other advertisers.

You can use the Quality Score diagnostic tool to identify where it might be beneficial to improve your ads, landing pages, or keyword selection.

**On this page**

*   [Calculate Quality Score](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118#calculate_score)
*   [Check Quality Score](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118#check_qs)

**Good to know about Quality Score**

*   Quality Score is not a key performance indicator and should not be optimized or aggregated with the rest of your data.
*   Quality Score is not an input in the ad auction. It’s a diagnostic tool to identify how ads that show for certain keywords affect the user experience.

* * *

## [](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118)How it’s calculated

Quality Score is calculated based on the combined performance of 3 components:

*   **Expected clickthrough rate (CTR)**: The likelihood that your ad will be clicked when shown.
*   **Ad relevance**: How closely your ad matches the intent behind a user's search.
*   **Landing page experience**: How relevant and useful your landing page is to people who click your ad.

Each component is evaluated with a status of “Above average,” “Average,” or “Below average.” This evaluation is based on a comparison with other advertisers whose ads showed for the exact same search over the last 90 days.

A broad match keyword may have a Quality Score even though it has no impressions as long as there is a corresponding exact match keyword with impressions in the last 90 days. If there are impressions for searches that exactly match a broad match keyword through an exact match keyword in the same ad group, this will report the same Quality Score for both of the keywords.

If one of these components has a status of “Average” or “Below average”, this may indicate an opportunity to make improvements. Learn more about [5 ways to use Quality Score to improve your performance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167130).

### Keep in mind

*   Quality Score is based on **historical impressions for exact searches**of your keyword, therefore changing keyword match types will not impact Quality Score.
*   If you notice a “—” in the Quality Score column, it means there aren't enough searches that exactly match your keywords to determine a keyword’s Quality Score. To help gather traffic data and resolve this status: 
    *   **Use Keyword Planner to discover higher-volume keywords:** Identify relevant search terms with sufficient search volume.
    *   **Broaden match types:** While match types don't change how your Quality Score is calculated, broadening them helps your keyword participate in more auctions, increasing the chances of gathering enough exact-match search data to generate a score.

*   There are factors related to your ad quality that might not be captured by Quality Score. These factors include, but are not limited to: 
    *   Devices used in search
    *   Location of user
    *   Time of day
    *   Assets

*   Information obtained from any of Google's various [crawlers](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/advanced/crawling/overview-google-crawlers)may be used to assess ad quality, which can be reflected through Quality Score.

* * *

## [](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118)How to check your Quality Score

1.   Go to [**Keywords**](https://ads.google.com/aw/keywords) within the **Campaigns** menu ![Image 1: Campaigns Icon](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/PYU3UjHzepAdY-dWS9ObIzq9WgLGS0SZeJS1hQ0Be3fxCIUQZaWCrR4HoYqriXSEbQ=w40).
2.   In the upper right corner of the table, select the columns icon ![Image 2: A picture of the Google Ads columns icon](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/poJPSxxmyG5nyGxTbdiUmvgDuTZF5IHNddHCp2_gGuax6_nG4coJefjn7KKwJfWu4c8=w50) .
3.   Under “Modify columns for keywords”, select the drop-down arrow beside “All columns” and open the Quality score section.
4.   To add the current Quality Score and its component statuses as new columns in the keyword reporting table, select any of the following: 
    *   Quality Score
    *   Landing Page Exp.
    *   Exp. CTR
    *   Ad Relevance

5.   To view past Quality Score stats for the reporting period you’re looking at, choose any of the following metrics. To add past Quality Score data and its component statuses as new columns in the keyword reporting table, select the following: 
    *   Quality Score (hist.)
    *   Landing Page Exper. (hist.)
    *   Ad Relevance (hist.)
    *   Exp. CTR. (hist.) You can view the change in daily scores by segmenting your table by day. 

6.   Select **Apply**.

* * *

### Related links

*   [5 ways to use Quality Score to improve your performance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167130)
*   [About ad quality](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/156066)

### [What Animal Care and Service Workers Do](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-2)

Animal care and service workers attend to or train animals.

### [Work Environment](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-3)

Animal care and service workers are employed in a variety of settings, including kennels, zoos, stables, animal shelters, pet stores, veterinary clinics, and aquariums. Some parts of the job may be physically or emotionally demanding, and workers risk injury when caring for animals.

### [How to Become an Animal Care and Service Worker](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-4)

Animal care and service workers typically have a high school diploma or equivalent and learn the occupation on the job. Many employers prefer to hire candidates who have experience working with animals.

### [Pay](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-5)

The median annual wage for animal caretakers was $35,360 in May 2025.

The median annual wage for animal trainers was $39,990 in May 2025.

### [Job Outlook](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#tab-6)

Overall employment of animal care and service workers is projected to grow 11 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.

About 69,400 openings for animal care and service workers are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.

## What Animal Care and Service Workers Do[About this section](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/animal-care-and-service-workers.htm#TB_inline?height=325&width=325&inlineId=about-what-they-do)

![Image 1: Animal care and service workers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/images/2698.jpg)

Pet sitters care for pets while the owner is at work or on vacation.

Animal care and service workers attend to or train animals. Working with pets and other nonfarm animals, these caretakers and trainers feed, groom, and exercise the animals or teach them to respond to human commands.

### Duties

Animal care and service workers typically do the following:

*   Give food and water to animals
*   Clean equipment and the living spaces of animals
*   Monitor animals and record details of their diet, physical condition, and behavior
*   Examine animals for signs of illness or injury
*   Exercise animals
*   Bathe animals, trim nails, clip hair, and attend to other grooming needs
*   Train animals to obey or to behave in a specific manner

The following are types of animal care and service workers:

**_Animal trainers_** teach animals a variety of skills, such as obedience, performance, riding, security, and assisting people with disabilities. They familiarize animals with human voices and contact, and they teach animals to respond to commands. Most animal trainers work with dogs and horses, but some work with marine mammals, such as dolphins. Trainers teach a variety of skills. For example, some train dogs to guide people with disabilities, or they may train animals for a competition.

**_Groomers_** specialize in maintaining a pet’s ap
